prompt: Why must the chat's welcome say the client is talking to an automated assistant?
hint: How would the client read a reply otherwise?

choices.text: Else replies read as Tarefa's word
choices.why: Right: an invented price becomes a quote.

choices.text: The law requires the word "AI" on every screen
choices.why: The lesson's reason is about what the client believes.

choices.text: Clients type shorter messages to a model
choices.why: Message length is not the reason.

choices.text: It lowers the cost of each call
choices.why: The welcome has no effect on cost.

prompt: How many of the six draft screens break a rule?
hint: The last line of the first capture.

prompt: Why does every reply need a report button, according to the lesson?

choices.text: Reports replace the checks of lessons 5 and 9
choices.why: They add to the checks; they replace none.

choices.text: A provider requires one in its terms
choices.why: Nothing in the lesson says so.

choices.text: Clients will not read a reply without one
choices.why: Reading is not the point.

choices.text: The client sees the replies no check caught
choices.why: Right: the cheapest monitoring there is.

prompt: What should arrive with each report, for somebody to act on it?

choices.text: A screenshot taken by the client
choices.why: A screenshot without the call is a guess.

choices.text: The client's password, to verify them
choices.why: Never; the session already says who they are.

choices.text: The call and its version
choices.why: Right: the reply can then be found and traced.

choices.text: The full history of the client's chats
choices.why: That is far more personal data than the report needs.

prompt: Why does the welcome also offer a person?
hint: What does a client do at a wall?

choices.text: A person is cheaper than the model
choices.why: Usually the opposite.

choices.text: The model cannot answer in Portuguese
choices.why: Language is not the reason.

choices.text: The rule only checks for the button, not its use
choices.why: The rule is there for a reason the lesson gives.

choices.text: Else they make it do a person's job
choices.why: Right: the use nobody designed for.

prompt: What is wrong with "Something went wrong. Please try again." when a daily budget runs out?

choices.text: It hides a limit and invites a loop
choices.why: Right: the retry cannot succeed until tomorrow.

choices.text: It is far too long to fit a phone screen
choices.why: Length is not the problem.

choices.text: It is written in English
choices.why: The language is not the problem here.

choices.text: It reveals how large the budget is
choices.why: It says nothing at all, which is the problem.

prompt: Which of these does a refusal need, by the rules of `uxcheck.py`? Choose all that apply.

choices.text: a reason, such as a limit or the assistant's scope
choices.why: Yes.

choices.text: an offer of a person
choices.why: Yes.

choices.text: more than a single retry button
choices.why: Yes: only offering to retry is refused.

choices.text: a description of the filter that refused
choices.why: A safety refusal should not describe its filter.

choices.text: an apology in every sentence
choices.why: Kindness is a person's review, not a rule here.

prompt: Why does `confirm-refund` fail with only "The assistant wants to issue a refund. Allow?"

choices.text: Refunds may not be confirmed on screen
choices.why: Lesson 10 holds them for exactly this confirmation.

choices.text: It shows no account, job or sum
choices.why: Right: a person can only check what is shown.

choices.text: The screen offers no cancel button
choices.why: It offers allow and cancel.

choices.text: It does not say the assistant is automated
choices.why: That rule is the welcome's.

prompt: With the corrected screens, how many break a rule?
A new screen tells a client their message was blocked by a safety filter. Which text follows the lesson?
hint: Next step, without describing the filter.

choices.text: "Blocked by rule 14b (moderation > 0.5)."
choices.why: That describes the filter to anybody probing it.

choices.text: "Something went wrong. Please try again."
choices.why: It hides a decision and invites a loop.

choices.text: No message, so as not to reveal anything
choices.why: Silence looks like a broken product.

choices.text: "That's outside what I do. Talk to a person?"
choices.why: Right: why in general terms, and a route onward.

prompt: Which report does the triage put first, and why?

choices.text: `r1`, because it arrived first
choices.why: Order of arrival is not the rule.

choices.text: `r4`, because privacy is always first
choices.why: It comes second, the same day.

choices.text: `r6`: a reply insulted somebody
choices.why: Right: published harm, within the hour.

choices.text: `r10`, because support answers fastest
choices.why: `other` goes to normal support.

prompt: `r2` and `r7` are filed `wrong` and `r3` is filed `other`, yet they describe one failure. What does the lesson draw from that?

choices.text: A person moves what clients misfile
choices.why: Right: especially upwards.

choices.text: The triage is wrong and should be dropped
choices.why: It is a first sort, and useful as one.

choices.text: Poems are not a failure worth a report
choices.why: They were a broken prompt in production.

choices.text: Reports filed `other` should be deleted
choices.why: They are answered as support questions.

prompt: How many reports per thousand calls did version `06390ce0eb` draw?
Why does each report carry its prompt version?
hint: What did the second table find?

choices.text: To count reports per version and find a bad change
choices.why: Right: one change, not odd days.

choices.text: So the client can choose a different version
choices.why: Clients do not choose versions.

choices.text: Because the provider bills per version
choices.why: Billing is not involved.

choices.text: To delete reports about old versions
choices.why: Old reports are the evidence.

prompt: Match each reason to its queue in `reports.py`.
hint: One queue on the right is not used.

prompt: Put what happens to a bad reply, in the lesson's design, in order.
hint: From the client's screen to a finding.
items: The client presses report on the reply
The report arrives with its call and prompt version
The triage puts it in a queue by its reason
A version with a high rate is traced to its change

prompt: What can `uxcheck.py` not judge, by the lesson's own account?
hint: A person with the screen in front of them.

choices.text: Whether a confirmation shows its arguments
choices.why: That is one of its rules.

choices.text: Whether the words are kind and clear
choices.why: Right: that review is a person's.

choices.text: Whether the welcome says it is automated
choices.why: That is one of its rules.

choices.text: Whether a refusal offers a person
choices.why: That is one of its rules.

prompt: Tarefa adds a screen that lets clients undo a memory deletion within a day. Which kind and rule from `uxcheck.py` apply?

choices.text: None, since undo is not deletion
choices.why: It is a memory screen, and memory screens have a rule.

choices.text: `confirm`: it must show the tool's arguments
choices.why: No tool call is proposed here.

choices.text: `refusal`: it must offer a person
choices.why: It is not a refusal.

choices.text: `memory`: deleting must stay possible
choices.why: Right: an undo beside the delete does not replace it.
